title: Cheap-LoRA fixed columns versus shared Mirror subspace views
hypothesis: A shared learned column basis with compact per-task Mirror coordinates can recover aligned adapter deltas more efficiently than fixed/random Cheap-LoRA columns, while independent task subspaces may require private factors.
physical_object: one frozen 32×32 weight matrix and shared column basis
mirror_coordinate: per-task address selecting/weighting one or more shared basis columns

development.allowed: validate subspace generation, fit, payload serialization and task-interference measures

success_gate: Aligned: Mirror NRMSE <=0.01 and <=70% bytes of per-task Cheap-LoRA, with >=10% improvement over generic shared coefficients at matched bytes to claim Mirror-specific value.
failure_gate: Mirror NRMSE >0.05, no reduction over fixed cLA at matched quality, or generic coefficient equivalence.
boundaries: PA29 Cheap-LoRA is mandatory direct prior-art control
Subspace combination count is not capacity
